tools.name: bash_background
tools.label: Bash (background)
tools.description: Run a shell command in the background; returns a task id at once. You are notified once when it exits (exit code, last lines, output file); do not poll, sleep, or delegate a subagent to wait. Use it for anything over about 30 seconds or of unknown duration (CI, builds, long tests, servers); quick checks stay in bash. Make the command's exit the event, e.g. `gh run watch <run-id> --exit-status`. Read its output file with the read tool. task_stop stops it. At most 25 run at once.

command.description: Shell command to run in the background, in the session working directory.

label.description: Short human-readable label, e.g. 'CI for PR 1834'.

tools.name: monitor
tools.label: Monitor
tools.description: Run a command in the background and get each output line as an event while it runs. Do not poll or sleep between events. E.g. `tail -f app.log | grep --line-buffered ERROR`. For one result when a command ends, use bash_background instead. Lines within 200 ms arrive as one notice (at most 20). timeout_seconds is mandatory (1-1800); it stops at the timeout or past 120 lines in 60s, so filter the command's output. task_stop stops it.

command.description: Shell command whose output lines are events, run in the session working directory.

timeout_seconds.description: Mandatory: stop the monitor after this many seconds.

label.description: Short human-readable label, e.g. 'CI checks for PR 1842'.

tools.name: task_list
tools.label: List background tasks
tools.description: List this session's background tasks (commands, monitors, sub-agents) with status and output file.

tools.name: task_result
tools.label: Task result
tools.description: Read a background task's status and result: a command's exit and last lines, or a sub-agent's answer. Its end arrives as a message anyway; do not poll.

id.description: The task's id, e.g. job-1 or agent-2.

tools.name: task_stop
tools.label: Stop a task
tools.description: Stop a background task (a command with its process tree, or a sub-agent). A stopped task sends no notice.

id.description: The task's id, e.g. job-1 or agent-2.
